_comment: SCENE FILE — the publisher splash, and the scene the application BOOTS into. One file per scene, named <Name>.scene.json; the engine indexes this whole folder at startup, so THE FOLDER LISTING IS THE ROSTER and the scene's id is its file name (TegLogo) — never restated inside the document. `boot` marks the one scene that starts the application: exactly one file in this folder may claim it, and zero or two is a loud failure at boot. `behaviour` names the registered Rust behaviour that PLAYS this scene (the engine knows behaviours, not scenes — adding a scene is data, adding a new KIND of scene is Rust), and `params` is that behaviour's own configuration: `splash` fades one image in/holds/out, fires the result `done`, and is skippable with click / Space / Escape. `image` is relative to the content root. `exits` maps a FIRED RESULT NAME to the scene it goes to (`mode`: replace | replace_root | push, default replace) — so reordering the intro, or booting straight to the menu, is editing this file, not recompiling. NO `tree` YET: the splash's visuals are the immediate-mode `scripts/logo.lua` timeline over the image above, fitted by the image's runtime pixel size — there is no component tree to author until that draw converts, and authoring a decorative one the engine does not read would be dead data.
